notes: Kyushu and Tsushima: the winter birds a birder drives to Kyushu for. About 15,000 Hooded and White-naped Cranes winter at Izumi, the Saga and Fukuoka tidal flats hold Black-faced Spoonbill and Saunders's Gull, and Tsushima is a stopover for Asian migrants (buntings, flycatchers, Daurian Jackdaw, Rook). A small pack on purpose: Kyushu shares most of its birds with the Honshu trip. The GeoModel scores these specialists low (Hooded Crane 0.17), so the list is hand-picked from eBird's lists for Izumi, Saga, Fukuoka and Tsushima. Mongolian Gull (casgul4) is not in the country species table for Japan and was left out. Photos are review-agent picks from unreviewed candidates (not approved on production): check them on /trip-photos. Shaky picks: Black-faced Bunting (winter/female plumages); Ochre-rumped Bunting (Reed Bunting-group ID doubt); Saunders's Gull (mostly small/distant shots); Oriental Stork (mostly distant/flight).
